[ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | They want each person given scrolls to unroll and read, like letters exchanged between people.

[ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | They reportedly demanded a personal heavenly letter addressed by God to each of them and commanding them to follow the Prophet, paralleling their demand for a book to read. | mentions 17:93, 6:7

[ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Their precedent was a claim that Israelites awoke with their sin and its expiation written above them; this demand differs from the open, spread pages unless those are understood as exposed writings, yielding the same basic idea.

[ELMALILI:74:32-56#3/r4] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | reports | Their demand for separately distributed pages may mean each wants an individually addressed reminder and invitation, perhaps with personalized tasks or benefits, or each wants to be a prophet.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The plural may mean that every command or prohibition for each person would need its own separate document.

[TABATABAI:74:49-52/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | After the preceding threat and promise, the passage presents as astonishing the rejection of the Qur'an's reminder and recoil from manifest truth: they should believe, yet seek individual revelation instead.
